subject.title: feat: add linux/riscv64 Docker image to multi-platform build

question: Should OpenClaw officially publish a best-effort standalone `linux/riscv64` image, with separate Dockerfile and Node provenance, while keeping default multi-arch manifests limited to amd64 and arm64?
rationale: This is a new release-supported architecture rather than a repair to an established contract; the maintainer must choose the acceptable availability, provenance, and support boundary.

options.title: Sponsor standalone riscv64 publishing
options.body: Review the active PR with its separate tag, documentation, and non-blocking workflow boundary, then land it if its supply-chain path is accepted.

options.title: Defer official image support
options.body: Keep the issue open but decline release publication until a maintained riscv64 base-image and provenance strategy is available.

options.title: Broaden the default manifest later
options.body: Accept standalone tags first and evaluate adding riscv64 to default manifests only after the architecture has stable release and attestation support.

recommendation.title: Sponsor standalone riscv64 publishing
recommendation.body: Review the active PR with its separate tag, documentation, and non-blocking workflow boundary, then land it if its supply-chain path is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Docker release, attestation, and runtime maintenance makes this the strongest available routing signal for the release-policy decision.
